cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A message queue is a buffer between services: a producer writes a message, the queue stores it durably, and consumers process it later at their own pace. AWS SQS, RabbitMQ and Azure Service Bus are examples.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: It decouples services so one being down does not break the other, absorbs traffic spikes as a backlog, keeps messages safe if a consumer crashes, and scales by adding consumers. Use it for work that does not need to finish inside the user's request: emails, video processing, order fulfilment.

questions.q: Is a queued message guaranteed processed exactly once and in order?
questions.a: Usually neither unless you design for it. Most queues are at-least-once, so a crash before ack causes redelivery.

questions.q: What does a queue do during a traffic spike?
questions.a: Absorbs it as a backlog that consumers work through at their own pace.

questions.q: Give work suited to a queue.
questions.a: Anything outside the user's request, like emails, video processing or order fulfilment.
